messages:
lucas (support): FYI AcmeCorp is reporting p99 regressions and some 502/504s since ~03:00 UTC. p95 looks fine, p99 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.8s. customer says 'sometimes just hangs then fails'. request ids: r-8a3f, r-8a40, r-8a4a. linking logs: https://logs.internal/r-8a3f

nina (support): confirmed, saw same in our dashboards. errors are mostly timeouts and a few 401->retry->timeout flows. All small prompt requests (<=120 tokens).

maya (sre): tagging eng-runtime. quick question: did anything change to continuous-batcher config or auth proxy around 02:30-03:00? also can you paste a short span of the batcher hold/window metrics?

owen (runtime): we did a traffic-optimized roll at 02:45 — increased default continuous_batcher.hold_ms from 40 -> 120 to improve throughput for noisy workloads. also rolled an auth-proxy patch that changes token refresh retry timing (adds jitter + couple extra retries).

maya (sre): that lines up. longer hold window improves batching for medium-sized traffic but can hurt tiny/latency-sensitive requests — especially if arrival is bursty or if retries change arrival patterns. short requests waiting on a large hold window can produce tail spikes. auth retries can create late-arriving requests that extend the hold.

lucas (support): customer profile: many tiny requests at low concurrency (per-req qps ~0.5-2). so they see single-request tail impact not throughput gains.

maya (sre): can we get the following quick diagnostics: 1) distribution of batch sizes for the affected model in last 2 hrs 2) histogram of continuous_batcher.hold_ms exposures per request 3) top 20 tail trace ids. a quick script to query would be helpful.

owen (runtime): pulling now. snippet from metrics query:
```
time_range: last_2h
model: redwood-llama-13b
continuous_batcher.batch_size_p50: 4
continuous_batcher.batch_size_p95: 16
continuous_batcher.batch_size_p99: 64
continuous_batcher.hold_ms_p50: 40
continuous_batcher.hold_ms_p95: 120
continuous_batcher.hold_ms_p99: 120
requests_where_initial_status=401_then_retry: 0.7%
```
observed: p99 hold_ms at the new 120ms for many small requests. plus ~1% of requests had a retry chain that arrived late.

maya (sre): that confirms it: many tiny requests are getting the 120ms hold, plus late arrivals from token-refresh retries are being coalesced into already-waiting batches causing extra delay before dispatch and sometimes hitting upstream timeouts.

nina (support): customer also reported some 403s earlier which then retried client-side; could be client retry behavior compounding effect.

maya (sre): repro steps we used to validate locally (small script):
```
# repro tiny-request tail with configurable hold
for i in 1..200; do
  (sleep 0.$((RANDOM%30)) ; curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate > /dev/null) &
done
# run with continuous_batcher.hold_ms=40 vs 120 and compare p99
```
observed: with 120ms p99 ~1.6s, with 40ms p99 ~210ms.

owen (runtime): quick mitigation options:
- rollback hold_ms to 40 globally (fast, affects throughput gains)
- configure per-customer profile: keep 120ms generally but set AcmeCorp to 40ms via routing/profile (preferred short-term)
- bump per-request timeout tolerance for auth retries (not ideal)
- patch auth-proxy to reduce retry jitter for token refresh to avoid late arrivals (medium-term)

maya (sre): operational quickfix: create a canary routing rule to set continuous_batcher.hold_ms=40 for the tenant group that includes AcmeCorp and any other low-qps tenants. apply to 5 pods, monitor p99. I'll do the change if oncall approves. Also will add a short-lived fallback that bypasses batching for single-request traces with header x-bypass-batch:1 if we need zero-risk fix.

lucas (support): can we also whitelist by route when auth failures detected so retries don't cause extra waiting? e.g., if upstream status 401/403 return immediate pass-through and let client retry.

owen (runtime): good idea. we can add a small change: when auth proxy returns 401/403, mark the request as non-coalescible for 50ms so other waiting requests won't be held for it. quick patch ETA 3 hours.

maya (sre): immediate actions agreed: 1) create incident ticket INC-5123 (nina) 2) apply per-tenant hold_ms=40 canary for AcmeCorp now (maya) 3) runtime to revert global rollout if canary doesn't reduce p99 in 10m (owen) 4) runtime to add non-coalescible flag for auth-failure-paths (owen) 5) support to confirm with customer and keep them in the loop (lucas)

nina (support): INC-5123 created: https://incidents.internal/INC-5123. assigning oncall. notifying account team.

maya (sre): applying canary now -> will post metrics in 5m.

sre-bot: deploy started: apply config route acmecorp.hold_ms=40 -> pods: svc-01, svc-03, svc-07 (canary)

(5m pass)

maya (sre): canary metrics: AcmeCorp p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~220ms within 2 minutes on canary pods. overall cluster p99 unchanged.

lucas (support): customer notified, they're seeing improvement on their traffic routed to canary. they asked what's next for a long-term fix.

nowen (runtime): next steps: revert global change or make default hold_ms adaptive (route by qps/profile). we'll prototype an adaptive hold_ms with heuristics: if per-tenant qps<5 -> 40ms, else 120ms. also will implement non-coalescible for auth-failures. opening runtime ticket RNT-2338.

maya (sre): sounds good. I'll keep INC-5123 open until global rollout is rolled back or adaptive hold_ms is live. thanks team. :thumbsup:

lucas (support): great — closing loop with AcmeCorp, will keep them updated and escalate if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
